**What happened.** $NKE closed at $75.43 on 2024-07-05 [E5], after falling ~20% on June 28 — from $94.19 to $75.37 — the session after its fiscal Q4 2024 report [E18]. The trigger was the June 27 release: Q4 revenue $12.6B, down 2% reported; NIKE Direct down 8% reported; wholesale up 5% [E11]. Morningstar cut its fair value to $124 from $129 on a "projected mid-single-digit sales decline in fiscal 2025" [E9] — that guidance came from the earnings call, not the release. I could not retrieve the call transcript or the exact FY25 guidance wording; web search returned no live results here [E14].

**Did On and Hoka steal the lunch?** Partly, and the numbers support your mall observation. On grew 2023 revenue 46.6% to CHF 1,792M with a 59.6% gross margin [E7]; Deckers grew FY24 (ended March 2024) revenue 18.2% to $4,288M with 55.6% gross and 21.6% operating margins [E8]; HOKA wholesale alone rose to $1,126M from $926M [E27]. But scale check: On plus all of Deckers is roughly a tenth of Nike's $51.4B FY24 revenue [E11] — they're winning the premium running niche, not displacing Nike overall. Nike's bigger problem in the print was its own execution: digital sales fell 3% for the year, Direct fell 8% in Q4, and classic franchises (Air Force 1, Dunk, AJ1) are oversupplied per management commentary [E11]. Nike's own FY23 10-K flags exactly this risk: reliance on fashion/trend demand and retailer concentration [E12].

**Bargain or trap?** At $75.43 against FY23 diluted EPS of $3.23 [E21] and trailing FY24 EPS around $3.73 (Q1–Q3 XBRL [E4] plus Q4's $0.99 [E16]), you're paying roughly 23x last year or ~20x trailing — not distressed-multiple territory. The calculator was unavailable this session, so those multiples are my arithmetic, not tool-computed. Cash ($8.96B) roughly matches long-term debt ($8.93B) as of Feb 29 [E22], and FY23 free cash flow was $4.87B [E3]. The question isn't the multiple — it's whether FY25's guided revenue decline is a one-time franchise cleanup or a structural share loss. Morningstar's $124 fair value vs. ~20x trailing earnings frames the bull case [E9]; what would settle it: Q1 FY25 revenue versus that guided decline, and whether Direct stabilizes.

This is research, not investment advice.
